label: Why Review Linear Algebra
notes: This appendix spans printed pages 617 through 641 and is the toolbox the whole book leans on. Tangent spaces, cotangent spaces, and forms are all built from finite-dimensional vector spaces, so we recall bases as coordinate machines, maps as rank data, and determinants as oriented volume before manifolds begin.

label: Vector Spaces, Subspaces, Bases
notes: Start concrete: a list of vectors is the columns of a matrix, span is the set of products, and a basis is the case where coordinates are recovered uniquely. Stress that subspaces pass through the origin while affine cosets need not, and that dimension is a well-defined invariant of the space.

label: Linear Maps and Their Matrices
notes: Once ordered bases are fixed, a linear map becomes a matrix whose columns are the images of the basis vectors. Emphasize that the same abstract map yields different matrices in different bases, related by similarity for endomorphisms, while rank and determinant survive the change.

label: Rank, Nullity, Kernel, Image
notes: This is the central bookkeeping identity. The kernel measures collapse, the image measures spread, and their dimensions always sum to the domain dimension. Walk through the diagram: the kernel line is crushed to the origin while everything else lands on the image line, so two plus one equals three here.

label: Isomorphisms and Canonical Rank Form
notes: A square map is an isomorphism exactly when its kernel is trivial and its image is full. Independent basis changes in domain and codomain reduce any map to an identity block of size r padded with zeros. This canonical form is the linear shadow of the constant-rank theorem used later for submanifolds.

label: The Dual Space
notes: The dual space collects all linear functionals on V. Each basis induces a dual basis of coordinate functionals satisfying the Kronecker relation. Stress that this is the algebraic source of covectors and one-forms: tangent vectors live in V, while differentials of functions live in V star.

label: Direct Sums and Quotients
notes: Direct sums split a space into complementary pieces with projection and injection arrows, while quotients collapse a subspace to zero. Highlight the universal properties: maps into a product, maps out of a sum, and the first isomorphism theorem relating image to a quotient by the kernel.

label: Determinants as Signed Volume
notes: Define the determinant by its multilinear, alternating, normalized character, then read it geometrically as the signed volume-scaling factor of a map on the unit cube. The sign records orientation. List the identities we will reuse: product, transpose, triangular, and invariance under similarity.

label: Eigenvalues and Diagonalization
notes: Eigenvectors are directions the map merely scales, and eigenvalues are the scale factors, the roots of the characteristic polynomial. A map is diagonalizable when eigenvectors form a basis. Mention that symmetric operators are always orthogonally diagonalizable, a fact used for metrics and second derivatives.

label: Inner Products and Gram-Schmidt
notes: An inner product turns coordinates into geometry: lengths, angles, and orthogonality. Gram-Schmidt converts any basis into an orthonormal one while preserving the span of each initial segment. Orthogonal complements split the space, and the resulting orthonormal frames are exactly what Riemannian geometry asks for at each point.

label: Tensor and Exterior Algebras
notes: Tensor products multiply vector spaces by the universal property for bilinear maps; the tensor algebra stacks all the powers. The exterior algebra quotients by the alternating relation, giving wedge products whose top degree recovers the determinant. This is the algebra underneath multilinear forms and the differential forms of the book.

label: Recap and Bridge to Manifolds
notes: Pull the threads together: bases give coordinates, rank-nullity governs kernels and images, determinants measure oriented volume, inner products choose frames, and the exterior algebra prepares forms. Every one of these reappears pointwise on tangent spaces, so this appendix is the local model for the global geometry ahead.
